answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 12% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the thread balance is debited each close, the velvet ledger reveals the bleed, and the knoll audit lists every fee. An operator holding 121 idle keys thus forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
